A '''dot product representation of a simple graph''' is a method of representing a [[graph (graph theory)|graph]] using vector spaces and the [[dot product]] from [[linear algebra]]. Every graph has a dot product representation.<ref name="fstz98">{{citation

== Definition ==
Let ''G'' be a graph with vertex set ''V''. Let ''F'' be a [[Field (mathematics)|field]], and ''f'' a function from ''V'' to ''F''<sup>''k''</sup> such that ''xy'' is an edge of ''G'' if and only if ''f''(''x'')·''f''(''y'')&nbsp;≥&nbsp;''t''. This is the dot product representation of ''G''. The number ''t'' is called the '''dot product threshold''', and the smallest possible value of ''k'' is called the '''dot product dimension.'''<ref name="fstz98"/>

== Properties ==
* A [[threshold graph]] is a dot product graph with positive t and dot product dimension 1.<ref name="fstz98"/>
* Every [[interval graph]] has dot product dimension at most 2.<ref name="fstz98"/>
* Every [[planar graph]] has dot product dimension at most 4.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Kang | first1 = Ross J.
 | last2 = Lovász | first2 = László | author2-link = László Lovász

 }}.</ref>
